title: STRENGTHENING DIGITAL PANCHAYAT GOVERNANCE THROUGH EGRAMSWARAJ
body_text:
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP) under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) with the objective of strengthening transparency, efficiency, and accountability in the functioning of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) through digital enablement across all States. The eGramSwaraj application has been integrated with various digital governance platforms to enhance planning, financial management and service delivery in Panchayati Raj Institutions. The major integrations are as follows:
Public Financial Management System (PFMS): For online fund management, accounting and end-to-end digital payments to vendors and beneficiaries. Government e-Marketplace (GeM): To facilitate procurement of goods and services by Panchayati Raj Institutions in a transparent and efficient manner. BSNL: To enable panchayat to apply for new internet connection and bill payment of BharatNet connection through eGramSwaraj. BHASHINI: To provide multilingual and AI-enabled language translation and voice-based services for improved accessibility of the platform. India Meteorological Department (IMD): To provide weather-related information for supporting local planning and decision-making by Panchayati Raj Institutions.
These integrations have been made available through the eGramSwaraj platform for all States and expected to benefit all Gram Panchayats across the country using the eGramSwaraj platform.
Further, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj launched SabhaSaar , an AI-enabled voice-to-text meeting summarisation tool, that enables structured capture and summarisation of Gram Sabha proceedings and supports monitoring of key parameters such as frequency and type of Gram Sabha meetings and participation. The platform captures agenda-wise discussions, decisions, and participation details, and the generated minutes are made available to Panchayat functionaries for review, validation and final acceptance. SabhaSaar has been made available to all States/UTs.
During the FY 2025–26, out of a total of 2,58,725 Gram Panchayats and equivalent across the States, 2,55,251 (98.65%) of them have uploaded their Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) on e-Gram Swaraj and 2,45,839 Gram Panchayats and equivalents (95%) have made payments amounting to ₹57,337 crore through the e-GramSwaraj–PFMS interface. Further a total of 1,35,956 Gram Panchayats and equivalent have used the SabhaSaar tool for automated meeting summarization and over 3,57,020 minutes of the meeting have been processed across States/UTs.
These initiatives are expected to enhance transparency through digital workflows and real-time monitoring, improve accountability by ensuring standardized planning and financial management processes, facilitate evidence-based decision-making through dashboards and reports, reduce manual intervention, and promote ease of governance by providing an integrated digital platform for planning, accounting, monitoring, and implementation of Panchayat activities.
This information was given by Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha on 12 th August 2026.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj informed the Rajya Sabha that its eGramSwaraj platform, under the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project of the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), has been integrated with PFMS, GeM, BSNL, BHASHINI and IMD to strengthen digital governance in Panchayati Raj Institutions. In FY 2025-26, 98.65% of Gram Panchayats uploaded their Gram Panchayat Development Plans and 95% made payments worth ₹57,337 crore via the eGramSwaraj-PFMS interface. The Ministry also launched SabhaSaar, an AI voice-to-text tool for summarising Gram Sabha proceedings, which has been used by over 1.35 lakh Gram Panchayats to process more than 3.57 lakh minutes of meetings.
enrichment.context:
The e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project is one of the 31 Mission Mode Projects under India's National e-Governance Plan, aimed at digitising the functioning of India's roughly 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats to improve planning, budgeting, accounting, monitoring and social audit. RGSA, the umbrella scheme for capacity building of Panchayati Raj Institutions, funds this digital push as part of the broader push for cooperative and 'Digital India' governance at the grassroots level, complementing the 73rd Constitutional Amendment's vision of decentralised local self-government. Integration with PFMS enables real-time, traceable fund transfers, curbing leakages, while linkage with GeM aims to bring transparency to Panchayat-level procurement, an area historically prone to corruption at the local level.

The SabhaSaar tool and BHASHINI integration reflect the government's growing use of AI and natural language processing to enhance citizen participation and multilingual accessibility in governance, particularly relevant given India's linguistic diversity and the constitutional mandate for Gram Sabhas to function as deliberative bodies under the Panchayati Raj system. IMD's weather-data integration supports local-level disaster preparedness and agricultural planning, linking climate information services with grassroots governance. Collectively, these measures indicate a shift toward data-driven, technology-enabled local governance, aligning with the Fifteenth Finance Commission's emphasis on Panchayat accountability and Sustainable Development Goal localisation efforts being tracked via Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs).

prelims_questions.question: The eGramSwaraj platform, mentioned in the context of digital Panchayat governance, is implemented under which of the following schemes?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project, which includes eGramSwaraj, is implemented under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA).

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following platforms/systems has NOT been integrated with eGramSwaraj as per the Ministry of Panchayati Raj's release?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release lists PFMS, GeM, BSNL, BHASHINI and IMD as integrations with eGramSwaraj; AEPS is not mentioned.

mains_questions.question: Discuss how digital integration of platforms like eGramSwaraj with PFMS and GeM can strengthen financial accountability and transparency in Panchayati Raj Institutions. What challenges remain in achieving full digital governance at the grassroots level?

Examine the role of AI-enabled tools such as SabhaSaar in enhancing citizen participation and deliberative democracy through Gram Sabhas. How can such technologies address linguistic and accessibility barriers in local governance?
